claims.explanation: Tipifarnib is a farnesyltransferase inhibitor whose selectivity is best explained by dependence on farnesylated RAS-family GTPases, particularly HRAS and KRAS, and by the presence of activating RAS-pathway mutations or RAS-driven transcriptional programs. Lines with HRAS/KRAS/NRAS mutations or RAS-pathway activation (e.g., NF1 loss) are sensitized, while lines lacking such dependencies or with compensatory PI3K/PTEN alterations are relatively protected. The observed enrichment of RAS-mutant gastric, pancreatic, colorectal, esophageal, and melanoma lines among the most killed supports this mechanism.

features.basis: Clinical validation of tipifarnib in HRAS-mutant HNSCC; HRAS is the canonical farnesyltransferase substrate
KRAS-mutant lines (GSU, T3M4, OV7, CL11, KPNSI9S) are enriched among most killed; KRAS requires farnesylation for membrane localization
NRAS-mutant melanoma line IPC298 is among the most killed; NRAS is a farnesylated small GTPase
NF1 loss hyperactivates RAS, creating dependence on farnesylated RAS; NF1-mutant lines (BICR6, LOXIMVI, KALS1) appear among killed lines
FNTA is the farnesyltransferase alpha subunit target of tipifarnib; higher expression may increase drug sensitivity
FNTB is the catalytic farnesyltransferase beta subunit target; expression may correlate with drug response
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT, bypassing RAS dependence; PTEN-mutant lines (786O, HEC265, KALS1, FTC133, ZR751) are enriched among least affected
PIK3CA mutations provide RAS-independent growth signaling; PIK3CA-mutant lines (HGC27, MKN1, SNUC5) appear among less affected
EGFR-mutant lung lines (NCIH1650, HCC4006) are among least affected, suggesting EGFR-driven lines do not depend on farnesylated RAS
BRAF-mutant lines (HEC265, SNUC5, IGR37) are enriched among least affected, consistent with BRAF/MEK-driven rather than RAS-driven proliferation
LMNA mutations causing progerin are farnesylated and tipifarnib-sensitive, though rare in cancer lines
